messages:
sara: Customer reports GET /internal/rr-eng returns NXDOMAIN from their app servers in prod VPC since 02:00 UTC. They say the public endpoints still work.

alex: Can you paste the error? Is it NXDOMAIN at app-level or from dig/curl?

sara: They sent curl: `curl https://internal.rr-eng.prod.svc.redwood:443` -> 'Could not resolve host: internal.rr-eng.prod.svc.redwood' and dig from one of their EC2s: ```; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> internal.rr-eng.prod.svc.redwood @10.0.0.2
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 12345
;; flags: qr rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0, AUTHORITY: 1, ADDITIONAL: 1
```

raj: Did they recently move/rename a private hosted zone or change VPC associations? NXDOMAIN usually means Route53 private hosted zone shadowing or missing assoc.

sara: They did a hosted zone rename this morning as part of a tenant consolidation. Ops docs say we re-associated VPCs post-rename, but customer claims their VPC never showed the new zone.

alex: @raj can you check our resolver logs for VPC association events for that account and zone id? Also ask customer to run `aws ec2 describe-vpc-peering-connections` and `aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id ZONEID` if they have perms.

raj: Looking now — route53 change shows: `ChangeInfo: {Id: /change/C-ABC, Status: INSYNC, SubmittedAt: 2026-03-15T01:58:12Z}` but the ListVPCAssociations for new zone shows only our infra VPCs, not customer's VPC (expected). I see an error in the audit: `VPC association request failed: 409 Hosted zone name conflict` around 02:00 UTC.

sara: 409 conflict how? They didn't have a hosted zone with same name, right?

raj: There was an overlapping private hosted zone in a different AWS account (internal migration account) with the same zone name still associated to the customer's VPC for a short window. That would cause split-horizon: resolver in their VPC can return NXDOMAIN if the resolver forwards to the other zone and it has no record.

sara: Customer also sent traceroute to resolver 10.0.0.2 and says responses are immediate, so not a firewall/egress allowlist. They also confirmed TLS certs unchanged.

alex: Ok next steps: 1) confirm which hosted zone is currently associated to their VPC (call out zone IDs). 2) If conflict, remove/replicate records to avoid NXDOMAIN during cutover. 3) Recommend TTL reduction for CNAME/A records next time. 4) Provide rollback plan.

raj: I ran `aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name` and `get-hosted-zone` for the name. Found two private zones: Z111111 (account A) and Z222222 (migration account). Z111111 is associated to their VPC but has no `internal.rr-eng` record (leftover). Z222222 has the correct records but is not associated. Change history shows reassociation attempted but failed due to the conflict.

sara: I've filed a support action with the migration team, asked them to disassociate Z111111 from the customer's VPC (temporary) so we can attach Z222222. They asked for customer approval.

alex: Meanwhile, workaround: customer can add a local hosts entry or configure resolver rules to point `internal.rr-eng.prod.svc.redwood` to the correct IPs until association fixed. Ask for OS and if they can tolerate the change.

oncall-bot: Reminder: Paging oncall-eng for manual VPC disassociation requires 30m maintenance window. Use `/page oncall-eng` if ready.`
